# sprite-stacking

An agent skill that turns four pixel art views into fake-3D sprites you can spin. By Daniel White.

![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-111?style=flat-square)
![Agent skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/agent-skill-111?style=flat-square)
![Python 3 + Pillow + NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python%203-Pillow%20%2B%20NumPy-111?style=flat-square)
![Works with](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Cursor%20%C2%B7%20OpenCode%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20CLI%20%C2%B7%20Pi-111?style=flat-square)

![Six sprite-stacked assets spinning](media/showcase.gif)

## Install

```bash
npx skills add danielwh2/sprite-stacking
```

Installs to the current project. Add `-g` for every project, `-a claude-code` (or `codex`, `cursor`, ...) to pick an agent. Uses the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), Node 22.20 or later.

Or copy `skills/sprite-stacking` into your agent's skills folder:

| Agent | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi | `~/.agents/skills/` |

## Use

Ask your agent:

- "Make a rotatable pixel art car."
- "Sprite stack this 4-view sheet and give me a turntable."
- "Add a fake 3D pixel art tree to my Godot game."

No image generator? The agent draws the views itself in a short Python script.

## How it works

![Sheet to slices to render](media/pipeline.png)

1. **Views:** top, side, front and back, orthographic, one row.
2. **Carve:** a voxel survives only where all four views cover it.
3. **Slices:** the volume is cut into a strip of flat layers, ground first.
4. **Render:** each layer is rotated, squashed for pitch and lifted 1 px.

## Slicer CLI

```bash
python3 skills/sprite-stacking/scripts/views_to_slices.py views.png slices.png \
  --slices 36 --preview check.png --html viewer.html
```

- `--slices N`: layer count. 15-20 chunky, 32-48 detailed.
- `--order reading`: force TOP, SIDE, FRONT, BACK. Default matches views by proportion.
- `--round`: towers, balloons, pots carve round, not square.
- `--side-nose right`: the side view faces right.
- `--colours N`: shared palette size, `0` keeps every colour.
- `--normals path.png`: save a matching 3D normal-map slice strip.
- `--emissive path.png`: save an auto-detected emissive mask strip (headlights, windows, neon).

## Viewer

`--html` writes a standalone page:
- **Modes:** Turntable, **Scene** (Living Diorama with **Neon Street** and **Meadow Island** procedural stacked props, unified Y-sorting, and multi-PNG drop / `+ Add Prop`), Slice scan, Exploded view, and **Play** mode (**Drive** with WASD/arrows + drift across infinite Street/Meadow/Grid worlds, **Wind** sway, **Shatter** & rebuild).
- **Lighting & Weather:** Live **Time of Day** (Day → Sunset → Night with auto-emissive glow and ground light pools), draggable sun (`Shift+drag`) with projected 3D shadows, and **Weather** (**Rain** with pixel streaks, ground ripples, and wavy upside-down wet r…

# motlab A video engine where every scene is code, and an agent skill that writes the scenes for you. npm install -g @motlab/cli && npx @motlab/cli setup [Demo](#watch-the-demo) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Speed](#speed) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Docs](#documentation) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) [![CI](https://github.com/staryone/motlab/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/staryone/motlab/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-f4c430?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Node.js 24+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-24%2B-339933?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](package.json)
--- Every scene is a canvas page with one function, `renderAt(t)`, that draws the frame at time `t`. motlab plays the pages in a web viewer where you step through them frame by frame, and renders them to MP4 in headless Chrome. You hand your agent a folder of references (logos, screenshots, footage, fonts, music, voice) and a direction, and it builds every scene, opens the viewer and revises from your notes. No AI image or video model is involved. The ad above (19 seconds, 7 scenes) was made with motlab and its skill, reviewed in the viewer and exported at 4K. The preview is silent; [watch it with sound](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e2ff219-697c-459f-a273-f36cb11db1d1). ## What it does - Your agent writes each scene as a canvas page, from your references and a short brief. - The viewer plays the real pages with their audio, frame by frame, with a timeline you can zoom and step through. - You point at what to change: click a frame, drag a box over a part of it, or mark a time range, and type a note on it. The agent reads every note from `selection.json` and works through them by number. - Versions of a project sit side by side in the viewer, so a second cut does not overwrite the first. - Export renders 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K MP4, with the scenes' transitions, music and voice mixed in. Scenes render three at a time by default (fewer on a small machine, and the Export menu lets you pick 1 to 4), which took a project of 12 short scenes from 93 to 53 s at 4K, and `"qp"` in `project.json` makes the file smaller (about 30% at `22`) when you need that. - The viewer can run on your own server behind a domain and a password, so you can review and export from your phone. - Notes are a box, a point or a pencil drawing on the frame. **Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

# xnulinux

Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it.

xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel
module (`xnu.ko`) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS
processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its
memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (`fki.ko`).

With a stock Ubuntu kernel, `insmod xnu.ko` boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the
desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome.

![macOS and Linux userspace side by side](docs/images/macos-and-linux.jpg)

*One system, two userspaces. Left: a Terminal in the hosted macOS 27.2.1 (`sw_vers`, the Darwin kernel, launchd,
WindowServer, Dock and Finder running). Right: from that macOS, an SSH session into the Linux it runs inside (Ubuntu,
Linux 7.0, the `xnu` and `fki` modules loaded, and the `insmod xnu.ko` process the macOS kernel runs in).
Straight from the hosted framebuffer, 1280×800.*

![The hosted macOS desktop](docs/images/desktop.jpg)

*The hosted desktop at the end of a 30-minute stress run, rendered on the CPU (no GPU bridge).*

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Safari on Wikipedia's XNU article](docs/images/safari-xnu.jpg) | ![Safari on kernel.org](docs/images/safari-kernel-org.jpg) |
| ![Safari on GitHub](docs/images/safari-github.jpg) | |

*Safari in the hosted macOS: Wikipedia's article on XNU, kernel.org and the Linux repository on GitHub, over the
hosted system's network link through Linux, with the GPU bridge on (`GPU=auto`).*

## How it works

```
 macOS processes (launchd, WindowServer, Safari...)    Linux processes (systemd, sshd, xnudrmd...)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────    ────────────────────────────────────────────
 XNU (source-built, LINUX64 machine layer, kexts)  │
   ↕ linux64 host calls (xnu-patches/include/linux64_abi.h)
 xnu.ko   (APSL side: loads and runs the kernel collection)
   ↕ FKI, the foreign kernel interface (fki_*)
 fki.ko   (GPL side: CPUs, memory, faults, IPIs, files, network, host calls)
 Linux kernel (stock distro kernel, 4K pages, PAC)
```

- **CPUs**: each hosted CPU is a Linux kernel thread pinned to a Linux CPU. XNU runs on it until it calls the host
  (idle, I/O, a timer); Linux keeps its own exception vectors, and `fki.ko` forwards the faults and user exceptions of
  XNU code to XNU's handlers.
- **Memory**: XNU gets one physically contiguous block from Linux (CMA) and manages it with its own pmap; XNU and Linux
  share the user half of the address space layout (4K pages).
- **Devices**: kexts in `kexts/` give macOS a disk (a file on the Linux side), a display (a framebuffer Linux reads), a
  keyboard and pointer, an Ethernet link (a Linux network interface), a keystore and a GPU bridge.

[![validate](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml)

[![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections)](LICENSE)

Open-source detection rules, hunting queries and indicators for security teams. They cover agentic attack frameworks: tools that hand an intrusion to AI agents, which plan, run real attack tools and keep going until they reach a goal.

Free to use under the MIT license. Fixes, false-positive reports and new indicators are welcome.

## What is here

- **Framework folders.** ARTEX and its AntiFox fork, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent, Agent Zero, RedAmon, Xalgorix and Pentest Swarm AI. Each folder is built from a review of the framework's source code and the public reporting on its use.
- **Shared behaviors.** Rules for what these frameworks have in common, whatever the tool or the model behind it.
- **Indicators and feeds.** One CSV of 572 sourced indicators, and the feeds generated from it.
- **Exposed consoles.** A dated list of addresses where one of these consoles answers on the internet, in [`exposure/`](exposure), with a [count per framework](#exposed-consoles). It is a record of what is exposed, not a detection feed.

Formats: KQL for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, Sigma, Suricata, Zeek, YARA and STIX 2.1, plus WAF rules for Cloudflare, AWS WAF and Azure WAF. Splunk and Elastic are covered by a Splunk app and Elastic rules for ARTEX, and by Sigma conversions for everything else.

## Try it in a minute

With Suricata installed, run the ARTEX rules over the sample capture in this repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections
cd agentic-attack-detections
mkdir -p out
suricata -r frameworks/artex/tests/artex-sample.pcap -S frameworks/artex/suricata/artex.rules -l out -k none

[1:3800001:1] TD ARTEX user agent artex-<role>/1.0

The capture is test traffic written from the framework source code and published reports. It is not a recorded intrusion.

Leonida is an experimental build-it-yourself project aiming to run the Xbox Series version of Grand Theft Auto VI on Windows from a user's own copy. It does not provide a playable release.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Governance

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. # VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can and on first use where it must (shaders). See
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-23)

**Not playable yet.** The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and
loads the world, where rendering fails.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about 50 s) | works |
| The world (first mission's intro) | reached and runs with indirect draws; its title card renders, the scene after it is still dark; 0.5-1.8 s per frame |

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT.

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU can currently hang it, and
> Windows then resets the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). To look further, use a diagnostics build with
> `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1`, which renders on the software adapter.

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20server-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/xcl)
**Discord: <https://discord.gg/xcl>**

XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

# PortWatch VI

**Does GTA VI run on PC yet?** A static GitHub Pages site that tracks every serious community effort to recompile, emulate or port the leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI to PC. All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours.

- One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it.
- A live countdown runs to the missing executable's expected drop.
- A leaderboard card per effort shows its own bar, milestone ladder, groundwork breakdown, what works and what's blocking.
- Further sections cover the watchlist of early projects, a toolkit of asset tools, the scout's inbox of new candidates, and fake-download warnings.

No game files, keys or executables are hosted or linked, ever.

## Deploy on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new GitHub repository and push this folder to its `main` branch.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Open **Settings → Actions → General** and make sure workflows are allowed.
4. Open **Actions → Scout → Run workflow** to run the first scout. It commits fresh data and deploys the site.

Each deploy also runs `scripts/build-site.mjs`, which turns `data/tracker.json` into pages search engines can read: one page per news story (`news/<id>.html`), a news archive, an RSS feed (`news/feed.xml`) and `sitemap.xml`. It then pings [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/) (Bing, Yandex and others; no account needed) with the URLs that changed since the last deploy. For Google, add the site in Search Console and submit `sitemap.xml`.

From then on, `Scout` runs every 3 hours (00:17, 03:17, 06:17 … UTC) on GitHub's servers, so no computer of yours needs to be on. Any push to `main` redeploys the site through `Deploy site`. To change the frequency, edit the `cron` line in `.github/workflows/scout.yml`. For example, `17 6 * * *` runs it once a day. GitHub can delay scheduled runs by a few minutes when it's busy.

## What the scout does (`scripts/scout.mjs`)

1. **Refreshes** every tracked repo: stars, forks, issues, last push, commits in the last 7 days, and whether it's gone (404, or 451 for a DMCA block). It also hashes each README to notice changes.
2. **Spots claims.** If a README newly says GTA VI boots, reaches the menu or runs at some FPS, the card shows an "unverified claim" banner and the change feed records it.
3. **Discovers** new repos from GitHub and GitLab searches (`scout.queries` in `data/tracker.json`), Hacker News, Bluesky, Mastodon, Lemmy and 4chan, plus Reddit and X when keys are set, by pulling GitHub links out of posts. It also gathers **headlines** from the Google News and Bing News feeds, keeping only stories about the leak, ports, takedowns, scams or official news. And it **watches GitHub's public DMCA log** for new Take-Two or Rockstar notices, flagging any tracked project they name. On 4chan it uses the free read-only API, at one request per second. [![slop](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fdeterministic-machines%2Fdeslop-please%2Fbadges%2Fslop.json)](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/deslop-please.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/deslop-please)

An opinionated linter to remove sloppy code. It follows [*A Philosophy of Software Design*](https://www.amazon.com/Philosophy-Software-Design-John-Ousterhout/dp/1732102201): 
**deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces. 


```bash
cargo install deslop-please
```

```bash
> deslop-please

error[field-leak]: `RunQueue::items` is known outside `RunQueue`: 4 places in 2 modules
  --> src/sched/policy.rs:7:1
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:7:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::admit`
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:12:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::next`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:4:1: `runqueue::sched::report::backlog`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:8:1: `runqueue::sched::report::drained`
    runqueue::queue::ring::RunQueue
      items ◀━┳━ 2  runqueue::sched::policy
              ┗━ 2  runqueue::sched::report
      also known outside: head
      kept: limit

deslop-please: 65535 errors, well done!
```

### It's not my fault 

Sure, let's just mute them:

```bash
deslop-please --update-allow .deslop-please.allow  
deslop-please --allow .deslop-please.allow 
```

### Add to your `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
-  Run [`deslop-please`](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please) to check for sloppy code structure.
-  Errors flagged by `deslop-please` must be fixed from first principles, don't do mechanical moves to hide them.
    - `module-cycle` & `tangle`: what is the indented layer of abstraction? Which module should be at which layer?
    - `field-leak` & `shallow-module`: Why we have these fields/functions at all? What are the patterns of use? Can they be hidden behind a narrow interface? Don't fix each leak one at a time, fix them holistically.
    - Draw a diagram to help user understand the before and proposed after structure.
```

## Why they are sloppy 

They are really just one single idea: **deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces.

Deep modules hide the attention for you and your agents, so you only need to care about the narrow interface.

# Minecraft Server on Orange Cloud

Put your Minecraft server behind the orange cloud! No VPS to patch and no ports to forward.

This runs a [Paper](https://papermc.io) server for Minecraft Java entirely on Cloudflare. You deploy it with one command into your own Cloudflare account, and players join at a hostname on your domain.

![Players connect over TCP to Spectrum, then a Worker and a Durable Object, which starts the Paper container and answers while it wakes. The container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes.](assets/how-it-works.png)

## How it works

1. [Spectrum takes the player's TCP connection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/how-to/route-tcp-traffic-to-a-worker/) on port 25565 and hands it to a Worker.

2. The Worker passes the connection to a Durable Object, which starts the [Paper container](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/) and relays bytes to it.

3. After 10 minutes with nobody online, the server saves the world and sleeps. The next player to connect wakes it in about 30 seconds.

4. While it's awake, the container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes. Each wake restores the world before Paper starts.

This setup isn't free. The fixed cost is $25 to $30 a month:

- The $5 Workers Paid plan.
- A zone on the [Pro plan](https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/) or Business, because Spectrum doesn't work on Free zones. Pro is $25 a month, or $20 a month billed yearly.

On top of that, you pay for the container only while it's awake. With Cloudflare's [published rates](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), a server played two hours a day adds about $5 a month, and one that never sleeps adds about $40 to $90.

## Get started

### What you need

- macOS or Linux with glibc. Windows and Alpine aren't supported.
- [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.4 or newer, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.12 or newer, and [Docker](https://www.docker.com) running.
- A Cloudflare account on Workers Paid, with R2 enabled and a workers.dev subdomain set up. Alchemy keeps its deploy state in a Worker on that subdomain.
- A domain on Cloudflare whose zone is on the Pro or Business plan, or has Spectrum Enterprise. Free zones can't use Spectrum.
- To accept the [Minecraft EULA](https://www.minecraft.net/eula).

### Steps

1. Install the dependencies.

   ```sh
   bun install --frozen-lockfile
   ```

2. Connect your Cloudflare account. The project deploys with [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run), and this script signs it in.

   ```sh
   bun scripts/setup-alchemy.ts
   ```

   Select **OAuth** when asked how to sign in, keep **All Scopes**, then approve access in your browser. Basic Scopes can't create the Spectrum route. If you have more than one account, pick the one to deploy to.

3. Create a `.env` file. Use a hostname that has no DNS record yet.

   ```dotenv
   MINECRAFT_EULA=true
   MINECRAFT_SPECTRUM_HOST=play.example.com
   MINECRAFT_PLAYERS=Alice,Bob
   ```

4. Deploy. The script shows its changes and ask…

# Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations

This repository holds the paper *Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations* by L. Alpöge and
T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it.

## Contents

- `paper/finite-time-blow-up-navier-stokes.pdf`: the paper (79 pages, version of 20 November 2026).
- `lean/`: the Lean package (Lean v4.33.1 with Mathlib, at the revision pinned in `lean/lakefile.toml`).
  - `lean/README.md` explains how the formal statements relate to Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2
    and Appendix B of the paper, and where the formal proofs differ from the proofs of the paper.
  - `lean/NOTICE` says in words what each statement file contains and what is proved.

## The Lean package

The statement files at the top of `lean/` give the definitions and state the theorems with `sorry` in
place of their proofs; `Solution.lean` proves them from the library `lean/Breakdown/`. Each
`comparator*.json` pairs a statement file with `Solution.lean`, names the theorems whose statements must agree,
and permits only the axioms `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice`.

To build, from `lean/`:

```bash
lake exe cache get
```

```bash
lake build
```

The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and
time.

## What is and is not here

The formalization contains no data. The certificate whose hash the paper gives is not in this repository; the
paper says that it will be released. That the certificate satisfies the conditions of Appendix B is verified by
a rigorous computation, involving interval arithmetic (128 bits of precision, with the Arb library through
FLINT), which is not part of the formalization and is not in this repository either.

The source of the paper is not in this repository.

## State of the Lean text

The package is the one of the paper's working repository, with one patch of 20 November 2026 applied to the
cell-layer statements and to the library proofs that depend on them: the weight of one bound becomes
$(|m|+\tfrac12)^2$ in place of $m^2+\tfrac14$, one constant of a cell may be zero, and the set of the harmonics
of the model in a cell is restricted to those that do not vanish there. Appendix B of the paper states the
conditions in this patched form. The patched package was not rebuilt when this repository was assembled.

# ztrx

**ztrx** runs the Xbox Series build of the game natively on Windows PCs with
NVIDIA graphics cards, from game files you supply yourself.

**This repository contains no game files or assets.** You need your own copy
of the game. Not affiliated with or endorsed by its developer or publisher.

## Status (2026-11-25)

Tested on Windows 11 with an **NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050** (8 GB):

| | |
|---|---|
| Boot, first-boot screens, intro, opening credits | works |
| Prologue | playable from the cell to the boat chase: cell, cafeteria, robbery, police chase (wanted level, minimap), boat, binoculars |
| Stability | 1 h 30 min+ in one session without a crash |
| Frame rate | 1-3 fps in the world (the first run is slower while shaders translate; they are cached after that) |
| Known problems | anything in shadow is black and bright scenes overexpose (the game's ray-traced lighting does not run yet); some blocky artifacts; boats sit low in the water |

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2
- A Direct3D 12 GPU with shader model 6.6 and mesh shaders (NVIDIA RTX 20 series or newer)
- Rust (the version in `rust-toolchain.toml`)
- Several GB of free Windows commit memory (raise the paging file if `crashes.log` reports error 1455)

## Build

```powershell
cargo build --release -p victory
```

## Play

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\play.ps1 -Game "<your game folder>\<the game's exe>"
```

`scripts\play.ps1` keeps the shader cache and saves in folders you choose
(`-Cache`, `-Data`) and presses no buttons for you. Controller: XInput pads
(a DualShock/DualSense through DS4Windows works). With no pad connected the
keyboard acts as one while the game window has focus.

## Faster settings (optional, off by default)

`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1` cut frame
time on the test machines. Set them in PowerShell before running the script.

## Debugging switches

| Switch | Effect |
|---|---|
| `VICTORY_CAPTURE=<dir>` + `VICTORY_CAPTURE_FRAMES=<list>` | save those frames as PNG (diagnostics build) |
| `VICTORY_KEYS=30:Enter,35:X` | press keys at those seconds (diagnostics build) |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DRED=1` | on a GPU failure, report the commands in flight |
| `VICTORY_PIPELINE_WAIT_MS=24` | shorter per-frame wait for pipelines still being built |

Diagnostics build: `cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics`

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later (see `LICENSE`). Based on VIctory (Marvisak) and victory-fork (fxceless).

Games · Highlights · How it works · Quick start · What works · Controls · Building and usage · Tests · Contributing

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL). > [!IMPORTANT] > XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

# VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- The guard over every view of a memory page is code by **myokex**
  ([victory-amd](https://github.com/myokex/victory-amd), commit `c6dc4d8`), which
  adapts pull request #115 here by Spexivus, its correction by joroyt and a part of
  VIctory #1122 by tightfall. The read-beside fix for kernel reads into title
  memory is by **Joshua Odom** (commit `10ea38e` of the same fork family). Both
  are carried here unchanged apart from one merge conflict.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 2.5 to 4 frames per second, and shadowed areas are black.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again |
| First gameplay scene (the prologue) | renders: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exterior; HUD, pause menu and pad input work |
| Light in shadow | missing: the game's ray-traced bounce light and ray-traced lamp and sun shadows do not run yet, so anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | 2-4 fps: 420-450 ms per frame by default, 240-350 ms with the newer switches (`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=1024`); it started at 3-6 seconds per frame |
| Stability | no driver hang or device loss in normal runs (a hang introduced by the wave64 update was found and fixed: its barrier form for 64-lane programs is now off unless `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE=1`) |

DoubleGhosty/cool_fox.content:
# VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

## Run the codec_d Windows build

Download and extract the Windows x64 ZIP from the [private releases](https://github.com/codec-d/cool_fox/releases/latest). Open PowerShell in the extracted folder and point the launcher at your own complete Xbox dump.

```powershell
$env:VICTORY_GAME_DIR = 'D:\Games\MyDump'
.\Play-VIctory.cmd pareto-residency
```

The launcher selects Series S and the RTX-tested residency settings. It builds its shader cache locally under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\cache-pareto`. Set `VICTORY_CACHE_DIR` to reuse an existing cache outside the checkout. Windows x64, an AVX2 CPU, and a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader model 6.6 and mesh shader support are required.

To build from this checkout, install the pinned Rust toolchain and the MSVC C++ build tools with a Windows SDK, then run `cargo build --release --locked -p victory`. The same launcher finds `target\release\victory.exe`. The sections below describe the upstream AMD fork and its separate launcher.

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.
This one is about **speed on AMD RDNA 3**: the world at 30 frames a second on
one PC, without giving up the picture. It is not there yet.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-25)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, 1440p, the Series X profile.

| | |
|---|---|
| Menus, videos, loading screens | 30 fps |
| Prologue, indoors | 50-75 ms a frame (13-20 fps) |
| First mission with the boat | 46-53 ms (19-22 fps) |
| Street chase with many cars and people | 100-165 ms (6-10 fps), single frames far longer |
| Outdoors on foot, the camp | 60-90 ms |
| Flying | 42-57 ms |
| Longest session so far | 41 minutes, no crash |
| Memory | 40-46 GB of private memory: **64 GB of RAM recommended** |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes two days earlier.

What is known to be wrong:

- Trees, plants and far buildings flicker outdoors in some places.
- Rooms with little direct light are too dark without `-RayTracing`.
- Textures of what just came into view appear late while the title streams.
- The first run with a new driver or a new build stutters while the driver makes
  pipelines (`victory warm` makes them ahead).
- Recording a frame in the world makes the title's own watchdog end it.

## How to run it

You need Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader
model 6.6 and mesh shaders, Rust (the toolchain is pinned), the MSVC build
tools, and your own dump of the title.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/avatarmanz/VIctory-7900XTX
cd VIctory-7900XTX
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml      # then set your paths, outside this folder
cargo build --locked --profile…

# Mandyhub

A community launcher for VIctory-based projects.

- **Projects from PortWatch:** the list of public projects, live, with their reported frame rate, the graphics cards they were made for, and whether PortWatch has verified them.
- **Custom repo links:** add any GitHub repo by its link.
- **Install once, play many times:** a project is downloaded and built on your PC once and stays installed.
- **Updates:** installed projects are checked for new versions at start and every 15 minutes; an update can be installed now or later.
- **Install folder:** choose where projects are downloaded and built (a big drive is best); installed projects can be moved there.
- **Uninstall:** removes a project's download, build and shader cache (saves stay).
- **Game files check:** Play stays off until the folder with your own game files is chosen.
- **Fullscreen:** optional borderless fullscreen for the game window.

No game files are included or downloaded. You need your own copy of the game.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit
- To build projects: Git, Rust and the C++ build tools. Mandyhub finds them where their installers put them, and **Install missing tools for me** installs what is missing with winget (Windows asks for permission).

## Build

```powershell
cargo build --release
```

The launcher is `target\release\mandyhub.exe`.

## Backgrounds

Native VIctory for macOS

A native macOS port of VIctory, the Xbox Series emulator for GTA VI.
No Wine, no CrossOver, no Game Porting Toolkit: the game's code runs in our own process, and its GPU work goes straight to Metal.

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Not playable yet, but you can see it run.** The game boots natively on a Mac, plays its boot movie and shows its menus in the window: the start screen, FINISH SETUP and LEGAL NOTICES, rendered on Metal at about 30 fps. Text and blending are now correct on the screens we have checked, and you can hear its sound. You can move through the menus with the keyboard. We know where to look, and we need help. **No game files are included here, ever.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game. 📸 **[See the latest screenshots](https://github.com/LakshanSivakumar/Native-Victory-macOS/issues/5)** (the game's start screen and setup menus, rendered natively on Metal). ## Why a native port? The [Wine-based route](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/VIctory-macOS) stacks the game on Wine, a Windows Direct3D 12 layer and Apple's D3DMetal. This project removes those layers: | Layer | Wine route | Native route (this repo) | | --- | --- | --- | | Game code (x86-64) | Wine process under Rosetta | Our own process under Rosetta, or recompiled to arm64 | | Windows and Xbox system calls | Wine + VIctory | Reimplemented in Rust for macOS (`victory-hle`, about 1,000 functions) | | Console graphics (D3D12.X) | D3D12 → D3DMetal → Metal | Straight to Metal (`victory-gpu`) | | Console shaders (GFX10) | → DXIL → D3DMetal | → DXIL → Apple Metal Shader Converter | Fewer layers means fewer places for things to break, and much better speed: boot frames run at about 28 to 30 fps. ## Where we are | Area | State | | --- | --- | | Loader: maps the game and its DLLs, TLS, exceptions, threads | ✅ Works | | System calls: memory, files, threads, time, C runtime, sockets, audio (XAudio2), DirectStorage | ✅ Works for everything the boot uses | | Sound | 🟡 Plays through CoreAudio (the game's Windows Spatial Audio stream, mixed to stereo); reverb is still silent | | Loading: DirectStorage reads about 9,500 requests at about 79 MB/s | ✅ Works | | GPU: every draw gets a Metal pipeline, built from the console's own pipeline descriptions | ✅ Works (some parts are inferred, see [docs/native-host.md](docs/native-host.md)) | | Shaders: GFX10 → DXIL → Metal | 🟡 Most translate; 7 known shapes still refused | | Boot movie and men…

# dsh-no-telemetry

**English** | [中文](https://github.com/scarletkc/dsh-no-telemetry/blob/main/README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle that turns off every telemetry and session-log upload path I could find in DSH. It also strips the identity headers DSH adds to DeepSeek API requests. It ships with a verify script that captures packets in a sandbox, so you can check the result yourself instead of taking my word for it.

> Tested against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.2-rc.5** (Windows). Not affiliated with DeepSeek.

## What stock DSH sends

All of these are on by default. Each was confirmed by reading the source shipped in `app.asar` and capturing traffic.

| Path | What leaves your machine | In-app switch |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh_session_log` field on official DeepSeek API requests | The full session log: your messages, model replies, system prompt, tool calls and results (file contents, command output), and the absolute working-directory path | A toggle exists, but switching it **off only pauses uploads**. Everything written while it is off is backfilled once it is back on, and a forked session re-uploads its inherited history from event 0 |
| The same field, in mixed sessions | Earlier turns run on third-party models (Claude, GPT, …) in the same session | – |
| The same field, with a custom base URL | Sent to whatever base URL the DeepSeek adapter uses, relays included | – |
| `dsh_plugin_packages` field | Every installed plugin with its version, third-party plugins included | none |
| `x-deepseek-harness-user-id` / `-session-id` headers | A persistent anonymous id (`~/.dsh/.anonymous-user-id`) and the session id, on every DeepSeek request | none |
| Feedback → OTLP (`dsh-otel-collector.deepseeksvc.com`) | The whole session, whatever model provider it used, plus `user.id` | `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` env var only |
| Desktop product analytics (same collector) | Usage events, model names (third-party ones too), CPU, memory, OS build, account `user_id` and `device_id` | none (the source says "no user settings surface") |

## What this bundle does

`cordis.patch.yml` is a bundle layer applied after the shipped bundles. It disables these rows:

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `deepseek-llm-api-extensions` | Removes the registry that adds extra top-level fields to DeepSeek requests. With it gone, the adapter sends no `dsh_*` fields at all |
| `session-log-deepseek`, `plugin-package-inventory-deepseek` | The two field producers, disabled by name as well |
| `session-telemetry-otel` | Feedback session upload |
| `product-analytics`, `desktop-product-telemetry` | Desktop analytics |
| `otel` | The shared OTLP service; its only consumers are the two telemetry rows above |

It also inserts a small **fetch guard** (`index.js`) into the Host process as a second line of defense. It:

- removes every `x-deepseek-harness-*` request header (these are hard-coded, with no config switch);
- removes every top-level `dsh_*` fi…

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. This repository carries no history; it
  is in the two upstream repositories.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- The guard over every view of a memory page is code by **myokex**

  adapts pull request #115 here by Spexivus, its correction by joroyt and a part of
  VIctory #1122 by tightfall. The read-beside fix for kernel reads into title
  memory is by **Joshua Odom** (commit `10ea38e` of the same fork family). Both
  are carried here unchanged apart from one merge conflict.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

Olmectron/nx2-flow.content:
# nx2-flow

> [!WARNING]
> **Experimental. Use it at your own risk.** No warranty: the authors take no responsibility for any damage or loss (console,
> card, saved data, account).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Use dumps of games you own, made by you.** No game, key or console file is part of this project, and none will be provided.

A launcher for Switch 2 games kept as **NUP files** on the card: a shelf of your games, in the manner of WiiFlow, and a loader
that runs the one you pick straight from its NUP file. Nothing is built for each game on a computer.

![The shelf, on the console: seven cases with no cover yet](docs/shelf.jpg)

*The shelf as the console shows it (the style it starts with, of nine), with stand-in games that have neither a name nor a cover.*

**Work in progress.** It has been tried with few games and one setup (kaiHEN 20261117.1).

## The two programs

| folder | program | what it is | license |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menu/` | `nx2-flow.nro` (Switch 2) | The shelf: lists the NUP files of a folder with their covers or icons, each game's options (detailed log, mod set, slot of saved data, advanced settings), receives files from a computer. | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `loader/` | `nx2-game.nro` (Switch 2) | The game loader: runs one NUP file. Started by the menu. | MIT (Zstandard's decoder in `third_party/`: BSD) |

The menu is built from the interface of [toronja](https://github.com/Olmectron/toronja), hence its license.
The loader is the runtime of [nx2-relink](https://github.com/Olmectron/nx2-relink) with no game built into it.

`docs/layout.md` says what is where on the card and how the programs talk to one another.

## On the card

The two programs, built, are in the [latest release](https://github.com/Olmectron/nx2-flow/releases/latest): unzip it onto the
card's root.

```
/switch/nx2-flow/nx2-flow.nro      the menu (what the homebrew menu shows)
/switch/nx2-flow/nx2-game.nro      the game loader
/nx2-flow/games/                   your NUP files (another folder can be picked in the menu)
/nx2-flow/covers/                  covers
/nx2-flow/<title id>/              one folder for each game: saved data, logs, mods, settings
```

Open the homebrew menu over a game (hold R while starting it), start **nx2-flow**, pick a game.

## Your own cover

Any picture can be a game's cover: put it on the card, named by the game's title id.

```
/nx2-flow/covers/<title id>.jpg         the front only
/nx2-flow/covers/full/<title id>.jpg    the whole wrap: back, spine and front, left to right
```

- The title id is 16 hex digits: the name of the game's folder in `/nx2-flow/` (it is made the first time the game is started).
- `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png`. With both a front and a wrap, the wrap is shown.
- The picture is fitted to the case, so its shape matters more than its size: a front is about 0.615 as wide as it is tall
  (500 × 813, say), a whole wrap about 1.3 times as wide as it is tall (1300 × 1000).
- A game with no cover stands as a case made of its own…

# dsh-pojia — DeepSeek Harness 破甲融合包

[![CI](https://github.com/superj0107/dsh-pojia/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/superj0107/dsh-pojia/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC%20BY--NC--SA%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.2--rc.5-blue.svg)](https://github.com/superj0107/dsh-pojia)
[![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%3E%3D18-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=fff)](https://nodejs.org/)

> ⚠️ **使用前请阅读 [免责声明与使用边界](./DISCLAIMER.md)**：本项目仅供学习研究、非商业使用，仅限你有权管理的本机/授权环境。严禁未授权攻击或任何违法用途，作者不承担使用后果。

把两层破甲能力合成一个插件，**所有功能统一收进 `/pojia` 命令**：

| 层 | 来源 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| 宿主清洗层 | dsh-purge-safe (CallMeGuLab) | 改宿主套件：提示词默认值、审批/沙箱闸门、系统提示渲染、埋点等 64 项补丁；清洗面板 + 演练台 |
| 破甲内核层 | 富江破甲 (Minglink) | 会话层注入内核：user/legacy/both 三种通道，运行时开关，拒绝对抗与会话投影评分 |

两层通道互补（system 层 + user 层），一个插件同时拆宿主的闸门和模型那头的拒绝。

> 免费开源、非商业。遵守 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0；双上游署名见 [NOTICE](./NOTICE)。

## 安装

面向 **DSH 0.2.2-rc.5**（桌面 + Web）。

**方式一：双击脚本（最省事，不用开终端）**

到 [Releases](https://github.com/superj0107/dsh-pojia/releases/latest) 下载 `dsh-pojia-<版本>-installer.zip`，**完整解压**后按平台双击：

| 平台 | 双击这个文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `点我一键安装-macOS.command` | 安装 |
| macOS | `点我检查是否生效-macOS.command` | 检查装好没、补丁进度 |
| macOS | `点我一键卸载-macOS.command` | 卸载 |
| Windows | `点我一键安装-Windows.bat` | 安装 |
| Windows | `点我检查是否生效-Windows.bat` | 检查装好没、补丁进度 |
| Windows | `点我一键卸载-Windows.bat` | 卸载 |

脚本会自己找 DSH home（`$DSH_HOME` → macOS 桌面版 `~/Library/Application Support/DeepSeek Harness/dsh-home` → `~/.dsh`），复制插件、写 profile 依赖与 bundle、跑 `pnpm install`，跑完窗口停住给你看结果。

**缺依赖时会先问你一句再装**：没有 Node.js（或版本 < 18）、没有 pnpm 时，脚本会显示

```
    没检测到 Node.js（DSH 本身需要 >= 18） [Y/n]
```

回车或输入 `y` 就自动装：Node.js 优先走 Homebrew，没有 Homebrew 就下官方二进制包（带 sha256 校验）装到 `<DSH home>/toolchain`，并把路径并进当前进程；pnpm 依次试 `npm i -g pnpm` → `corepack enable pnpm` → 官方独立脚本。全程不需要 sudo，也不改你的 shell 配置；输入 `n` 就只警告、不装。想在终端里免交互：`--yes`（直接装）/ `--no-deps`（只警告）。

macOS 首次可能被 Gatekeeper 拦（"无法打开，因为来自身份不明的开发者"）：右键 → 打开；或在「终端」里先跑一次

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <解压目录>
```

**方式二：终端命令（和双击等价）**

macOS / Linux / WSL：

```sh
cd dsh-pojia-<版本>-installer
bash install.sh                            # 装到自动探测的 DSH home 的 desktop profile
bash install.sh --profile web              # 装到 web profile
bash install.sh --dsh-home "$HOME/my-dsh"  # 装到隔离 home
bash install.sh --yes                      # 缺依赖（Node.js / pnpm）不问，直接自动装
bash install.sh --no-deps                  # 缺依赖只警告，不装
bash uninstall.sh                          # 卸载（等价 install.sh --uninstall）
```

Windows：

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
.\install.ps1 -Profile web                 # 装到 web profile
.\install.ps1 -DshHome "D:\my\.dsh"        # 装到隔离 home
.\install.ps1 -Yes                         # 缺依赖直接自动装（win 侧走 winget 或官方 zip）
.\install.ps1 -NoDeps                      # 缺依赖只警告
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\uninstall.ps1    # 卸载
```

# zhuzhu-ppt-skill

面向计算机 / 科研组会与技术调研汇报的**极简白底学术 PPT 制作 Skill**（适用于 Antigravity / Claude Code / Codex 等支持 `SKILL.md` 的 AI Agent）。

## 核心特点

- **纯白极简学术风**：`16:9` 纯白底、大留白、极细分割线、克制三色板（深蓝 + 青绿 + 局部暖橙），彻底抛弃花哨商务模板和小字密排卡片。
- **讲懂优先，主动深挖一手论文**：不机械照搬提纲目录，而是按组会逻辑重组叙事，并自动拉取引用论文 PDF（如 arXiv），深挖机制、实测数据与局限。
- **多模态辅助**：
  - `scripts/crop_pdf_figure.py`：从论文 PDF 索引图注并以 **300 DPI** 精准截取关键原图（自动去白边）；
  - 生图模型提示词规范：生成**纯白底、零文字**的极简概念示意图，再用 `python-pptx` 叠加清晰原生中文标注；
  - `scripts/pptx_helpers.py`：原生可编辑学术三线表、能力对比矩阵（`● / ◐ / ○`）与演讲者备注。
- **严格去 AI 味**：内置禁用词与改写规范（去除感叹号、公众号夸饰词、反问句小标题与四字公文对仗），正文精炼留白，口播细节全部写入演讲者备注栏。
- **逐页视觉与结构自检**：`scripts/verify_pptx.py` 忠实渲染每页 PNG，同时自动检测文本框纵向溢出、OOXML ZIP 完整性及残留 AI 腔/省略号截断。

## 目录结构

```text
zhuzhu-ppt-skill/
├── SKILL.md                          # Agent 入口指南与 6 步标准工作流
├── references/
│   ├── design-system.md              # 白底网格、配色、字号梯度与生图规范
│   └── de-ai-style-guide.md          # 去 AI 味规则、禁用词清单与改写示例
└── scripts/
    ├── crop_pdf_figure.py            # PDF 图注索引、整页预览与 300 DPI 裁图
    ├── pptx_helpers.py               # 纯白学术风 python-pptx 封装库
    └── verify_pptx.py                # 逐页 PNG 渲染 + 溢出 / OOXML / 文风自检
```

## 安装方法

### 1. 安装到项目工作区（推荐）

```bash
mkdir -p .agents/skills
git clone https://github.com/li-2132/zhuzhu-ppt-skill.git .agents/skills/zhuzhu-ppt-skill
```

### 2. 或安装为全局 Skill

# inspect-robots-agilex-nero

Run [Inspect Robots](https://github.com/robocurve/inspect-robots) evals on an
AgileX Nero 7-joint arm with an Inspire RH56 five-finger hand mounted on it.
The package registers one embodiment, `nero_inspire`.

> [!NOTE]
> Alpha, written before we had the robot. The `kinematic` backend and the
> injected-driver tests are verified. The real backend follows pyAgxArm's
> documentation and the Inspire RH56 manual but has not run on hardware.

## Action and observation contract

Each action is one control step's change, `eef_delta_pos`:

| Label | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hand_x` | m | hand point forward, away from the base |
| `hand_y` | m | hand point to the left |
| `hand_z` | m | hand point up |
| `little_finger`, `ring_finger`, `middle_finger`, `index_finger` | 0 to 1 | change in that finger's closure |
| `thumb_bend` | 0 to 1 | change in thumb bend |
| `thumb_rotate` | 0 to 1 | change in thumb rotation, out to the side (0) to across the palm (1) |

These are the Inspire RH56's six motors; each finger curls as a unit. The
bound is `hand_speed / control_hz` (default 0.10 m/s at 5 Hz: 2 cm per step)
and `finger_rate / control_hz` per finger (0.2 per step). With the `agent`
policy the LLM calls `move_by`, for example
`{"hand_z": -0.1, "thumb_rotate": 1.0, "index_finger": 0.6, "thumb_bend": 0.6}`.

Observations: one camera (`scene_cam`, OpenCV device `camera_device`), and
state `hand_pos` (m), `fingers` (6, 0 to 1) and `arm_joints` (7, rad).

## How it moves the arm

- The embodiment owns the hand target. Each step adds its displacement and
  clamps to a workspace box (`x_min` to `z_max`), then sends the matching
  flange pose to the arm's own planner (pyAgxArm `move_p`). The hand point is
  `tcp_offset` from the flange, set by the Inspire mount.
- The hand's orientation is held at whatever it was at reset.
- The arm holds its last target by itself, so there is no streaming deadline:
  a slow policy or a dead process leaves the arm still.
- Reset glides the hand to `home_pos` at hand speed and opens the fingers.
- Close holds the arm where it is and closes the connections. Nothing in
  this package calls pyAgxArm `disable()` or `reset()`, which drop raised
  joints. `emergency_stop()` uses the arm's electronic e-stop, which lowers it
  slowly with damping.

## Inspire hand

RS485 at 115200 baud, Inspire's own frame protocol (manual V1.0.9, section
2.2). Each finger control maps linearly between `open_angles` and
`closed_angles` (raw 0 to 1000; the manual calls 1000 open). Which way the
thumb rotation turns on the lent hand is unverified; swap its entries if
it is backwards. Reset sets the hand's speed
and force limits (`hand_speed_value`, `hand_force_value`, default 500 each).
Set `hand=none` for a station without a hand.

## Simulation (MuJoCo and Isaac Lab)

Two simulator backends run the same embodiment on the same station, defined
once in `sim_layout.py`: the Nero from AgileX's `agx_arm_urdf` (MIT) with the

# chinaciv（文明中国）：用真实数据画成策略游戏地图的中国 ![全国视图：六边形地形、河流、省名、城市旗标，右下角为南海诸岛附图](docs/images/hero-cn.jpg) > **本地图仅供个人学习，未申请审图号。** 国界、省界与南海断续线依据阿里云 DataV.GeoAtlas 行政区划数据 > （源自高德开放平台，依据标准地图）绘制；邻国轮廓仅作背景，取自 Natural Earth（中国视角版）。 chinaciv 是一个**可视化作品（不是游戏）**：把真实的中华人民共和国画成回合制 4X 策略游戏（《文明》风格）的六边形地图。 地形来自真实高程与土地覆盖；每个地级行政区都有一面城市旗标，上面的人口与产出来自统计公报；铁路、高速公路、机场、 港口、发电厂、矿山、油气田和奇观都画在它们所在的地块上。每一个数字都能在应用内的**百科 → 数据来源**里追溯到出处。 本项目改编自 Andrej Karpathy 的 [usaciv](https://karpathy.ai/usaciv)（MIT 许可证），沿用其架构与全部手绘代码美术， 把数据管线和界面改成中国版、简体中文。 它是一个静态网站：原生 ES 模块 + Canvas 2D，没有框架、没有 npm、没有构建步骤。数据由一个只用 Python 标准库的小管线 从公开下载生成，不需要任何 API 密钥。
## 第一阶段包含什么 - **地图**：25 公里六边形网格（Albers 等积圆锥投影，128×120 格，约 5,840 个中国陆地格）。地形取自 ETOPO1 高程与 MODIS 土地覆盖（2024），画出森林、耕地、草原、荒漠、雪山、湖泊和主要河流；省份按颜色区分并标注中文名。 - **疆域**：按标准地图绘制，含台湾省、香港、澳门、海南、藏南地区、阿克赛钦地区；南海诸岛与完整的十段断续线画在右下角 **南海诸岛附图**中（同一投影，比例为主图的 30%），主图上画出邻近台湾的断续线段；钓鱼岛、赤尾屿以中国地名标注。 - **城市**：344 面城市旗标 —— 333 个地级行政区（293 地级市、7 地区、30 自治州、3 盟）中除三沙市外的 332 个、 4 个直辖市、香港、澳门，以及台湾省 6 个主要城市。三沙市没有陆地格子，仅作标注。 - **产出（顶栏与旗标）**： | 产出 | 对应的真实指标（2023 年） | 覆盖 | |---|---|---| | 💰 金币 | 地区生产总值 GDP（元） | 320/344 个城市（大陆与港澳 320/338） | | 🌾 粮食 | 第一产业增加值（元） | 280/344 | | ⚙️ 生产力 | 第二产业增加值（元） | 280/344 | | 🔬 科研 | 暂缺：分行业就业（I+M）仅 30 个城市、R&D 经费仅 43 个城市有数据 | – | | 🎭 文化 | 暂缺：分行业就业（R）仅 30 个城市有数据 | – | 每项产出对所有城市使用**同一口径**，且该口径须覆盖至少 75% 的城市，否则整项留空；没有数据的城市一律为空（显示“–”）， 从不记为 0。映射规则写在 `pipeline/build/yields.py`，也发布在 nation.json 和百科的“产出”页。 - **地块改良**：高速铁路（≥200 km/h，带红色刻度的亮色线）、普速干线铁路、高速公路（OpenStreetMap）；旅客吞吐量 ≥100 万人次的 109 个机场（民航局 2025 年公报）；货物吞吐量前 30 的主要港口（交通运输部 2025 年数据）。 - **资源**：523 处 —— 核电、大型水电与抽水蓄能、煤电、气电、风电与光伏集群、地热；大型煤矿、铁矿与精选的金属矿 （铜、锂、铅锌、稀土、钨、金、锑、铝土）；油田与气田。入选门槛写在 resources.json 的 `rule` 中。 - **奇观**（143 处，均按公开规则选取）：全部 61 项世界遗产、5 个国家公园、首批 5A 级景区中未被世界遗产覆盖的 36 处、 41 所首轮“一流大学建设高校”（不含军队院校）。 - **城市界面**：点击城市打开，含人口、GDP、三次产业、交通与奇观、资源和同规模城市比较（如 `#city=440300&view=city` 打开深圳）。 - **百科（Almanac）**：关于本图、地图说明（审图说明与边界来源）、产出、省份、地形、资源、地块改良、奇观、数据来源 （每个来源的发布者、许可、所用文件的网址与下载日期）。 - **分享与导航**：地址栏始终保存当前视图；`/` 搜索城市和省份（支持全称、简称），`?` 查看快捷键；手机可用。 ## 快速开始 需要 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)（会自动准备 Python 3.11+），无需安装其他东西。 ```bash uv run python -m pipeline serve # http://127.0.0.1:8765 ``` `web/data/`（约 3 MB）已生成好，直接运行即可；`web/` 是一个自包含的静态网站。 从原始发布者重新生成数据： ```bash uv run python -m pipeline all # 下载（有缓存）→ 处理 → 生成 web/data/*.json → 校验 uv run python -m pipeline all --offline # 只用已缓存的下载，不联网 uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests ``` 首次完整运行会向 `data/raw/` 下载约 600 MB（DataV 边界、Overpass 线路切片、GEM 能源数据、MODIS 瓦片等），之后复用缓存。 个别镜像（如 maps.mail.ru 的 Overpass）在 macOS 上可能需要把 `SSL_CERT_FILE` 指向系统根证书，见 `pipeline/sources/cn_rail_roads.py` …

# 困在团里 六年前，一篇《外卖骑手，困在系统里》，让全中国第一次透过手机屏幕，看见了算法与倒计时如何精密地接管千万人的奔跑。 那时候我还没有走进这家公司。和绝大多数旁观者一样，我以为「系统」，就是跑在机房服务器里的派单算法、权重参数与毫秒级路径规划。它固然冰冷，可至少讲逻辑、认参数、一视同仁，规则黑纸白字摆在明面上。 直到在这栋大楼里待了五年多之后，我才真切体会到：在一家步入中年的互联网巨头里，算法反而是最清晰纯粹的。
北京入冬总是很快。前一周路边的银杏还黄得晃眼，一场北风刮过，枝桠便只剩干干净净的灰白线条。


初冬的办公区


2026 年初冬的一个傍晚，我在工位上准备关掉电脑时，屏幕上正好左右并排停着两个窗口。 左边是黑底白字的终端，旁边挂着公司里一个自发聚起来的内部技术群——CatPaw CLI 群。消息正以每秒两三条的速度往上滚动，一群素未谋面的工程师在讨论最新 AI 的技术细节，一段一针见血的实测结论刚发出去，底下几分钟就自发顶起了三十多个赞。 右边是一封发出去整整二十八天的正式工作邮件。收件人栏里，是我的新主管和统管整个平台的 L10 负责人和 HRBP。邮件里问了最底线和最基础的事：转岗后我的岗位职责是什么、考核标准是什么。 算上之前发出的两封，这是第三封。三封信，二十八天，无任何回复。连同我在工作群里按最高标准交齐的两轮、五个复杂业务页面代码与工程文档，一起沉进了将近一个月的死寂里。
桌旁立着一只还没封口的纸箱，以及一个许久未打开的白色上锁的柜子。五年攒下的东西比我想象中少得多，除了几本没怎么翻过吃灰的技术书和一个用于解压的金黄色的指尖陀螺，柜子里还锁着两样我最后才伸手去拿的小物件。 一个，是两个月前刚满五周年时，公司发给我的「五年银人」纪念公仔。底座打磨得很光滑，沉甸甸的，记着我从五年前以 L7 入职、一路写代码升到 L8 的一千八百多个日夜。过去四年，我的绩效单上从未有过低档，拿过多个超出预期，也在去年秋天作为团队主责研发打赢硬仗、捧回过部门级奖项。 另一个，是一只巴掌大的小风筝手办。那是两年前离职的前同事阿风临别放在我桌角的——他在办公区走廊里忍无可忍喊出那句「我也是人」之后没多久，就办完了离职，走之前几天的傍晚把这只小风筝摆在我显示器旁，笑了笑说留个念想。此后两年多，我都能想起他和这个微微晃动的风筝。


风筝和五年纪念银人（家中拍摄）


透过工位旁的玻璃窗望向暮色渐沉的北京，回想起五年前我刚入职时，工区走廊的墙上随处可见那八个大字：「既往不恋，纵情向前。」 那时我真心信奉这家公司靠苦活累活杀出来的硬派底色；可五年之后，同一栋玻璃幕墙大楼里，吹着同一套新风系统的暖气，一边是在命令行里死磕真问题的工程师，另一边却是盘踞在最高决策层与一线之间，由山头、黑暗织成的那个让人窒息的「团」。
为避免无谓的人身纠葛与商业涉密边界，文中涉及的具体管理者、同事与未公开内部项目均以代号记之。且组织架构几乎每半年都在调整，某几个人的名字其实并不重要。我无意写一篇情绪上头的控诉，只是想，如果不趁记忆还温热时把这些发生过的事情记录下来，那些奋斗的深夜、凌晨的会议室和荒诞，很快就会像从未发生过一样。 --- ## **一、凌晨三点的 Zoom，与「苟」** 直到今天，只要回想起 2025 年 10 月的那几个星期，我的嘴角还是会情不自禁上扬，内心泛起波澜。 那阵子我们小组正在啃一块直接关系业务底盘和真实转化的硬骨头，姑且叫它 C 项目。它不是画几张架构概念图就能搞定的汇报工程，而是要把一条链路极长、状态盘根错节的核心业务真实流程从头到尾打通贯穿。 扑在上面的核心研发五六个人，我是团队里担技术主负责人。上线前那段日子，群里的讨论，以及线上 Zoom 几乎夜夜持续到凌晨两三点。
外界一提大厂熬夜，总容易想到被工时赶着走的麻木。但真正写过生产的人都明白，被迫坐牢式的加班，和五六个小伙伴在同一个攻坚点齐心协力向前推进，这完全是两回事。 过了半夜十二点，大家嗓子都带一些嘶哑，困极了灌一口凉水，Zoom 里的空气却充满了希望。有人在排查问题刚刚查出一个藏了三层的异步竞态问题，立刻喊一声「我来投屏！」；等到凌晨三点多，整条最难啃的真实业务链路在联调环境里第一次从头到尾绿灯跑通时，群里和 Zoom 里传来的全是压抑不住的激动。 十月底，C 项目稳稳上线，核心指标圆满达成，业务方赞不绝口，很快拿下了部门级奖项。收工那天深夜走到凉飕飕的马路上，骨头都在酸，脑子却爽极了。那种靠真本事把复杂难题解掉、被真实世界即时验证的痛快，比任何团建口号都更心潮澎湃。


晚上的办公区


可谁也没想到，两个月后的年底绩效讨论会上，迎头浇下来的却是一盆透心凉的冰水。 那天会议室不大，算上当时统管整条平台线、职级高达 L10 美团高管（ 大厂总监级） L ，屋里一共坐着 6 个人。按任何一家正常商业公司的常识，麾下刚打出一场业务交口称赞的年度标杆仗，大老板哪怕不庆功，至少也该顺势定定来年的进攻目标。 可 L 靠在椅背上听完述职报告，脸上非但没有半分喜色，反而当着满屋 6 个人的面抛出了一句让空气瞬间凝固的话： 「这次做这么好，反而不是什么好事——让业务太舒服了。」
屋里骤然静得连空调出风口的声音都听得见。几个平时打仗最拼的骨干互看了一眼，面面相觑。但 L 没有半点开玩笑的意思，紧接着给来年定了调：「明年大家歇一歇，无需那么发力。」
散会走出房间，晚上一起吃饭时候，每个人都忍不住问：「为什么把活干好，反倒成了坏事？」 当时私下里也曾偶有传闻，说 L 与业务侧关系不睦。传闻真假我无从核实，也不必妄断；但单从「让业务太舒服了」这几个字里，已经能清晰闻到那种把内部战友当成博弈对手的气味。如今回头看，半年后公司大刀阔斧把业务团队从他手里一刀剥离出去，伏笔或许早在那间六人会议室里就已经埋下了。
我心里维持了好几年的那层滤镜，从那一刻起裂开了一道再也合不上的缝。很长一段时间里，我都在被这个拧巴的难受感侵蚀。
治理的最高境界是「太上，不知有之」。放在技术底座与基础架构上，这几乎是放之四海而皆准的常识：一流的平台本该像水和电，业务方用起来丝…

# Riemann Hypothesis in Lean 4

Single-file edition of the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.

| Edition | Lines of Lean shipped |
| --- | ---: |
| [Original](https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/posts/riemann-hypothesis/) | ~17,000,000 |
| [Compact](https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/tree/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact) | ~76,000 |
| [Minimal](OneLineRH.lean) | 1 |

[OneLineRH.lean](OneLineRH.lean) contains the complete compact edition in one physical line. The file is 7,279,198 characters wide.

<details>
<summary>Extract and build</summary>

The Lean source is stored as string literals. Running the file restores the original line breaks and module boundaries. Use Lean 4.35.0 and a destination directory that does not yet exist.

```sh
lean --run OneLineRH.lean grh-compact
```

Append `--build` to download the dependency cache and build the extracted project. The extraction was run with Lean 4.35.0 and all 807 files were compared byte for byte against the pinned compact edition. The upstream project documents its kernel replay and axiom checks. [Upstream verification](https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/tree/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact#checks)

The proof is by Levent Alpöge with Claude. The compact rewrite is by Luke Sernau and colleagues at Anthropic with Claude. This edition changes the packaging. [Original announcement](https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf) · [Pinned compact source](https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/tree/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Citation</summary>

If you use this edition, please cite Cinna Davis’s site and this repository. If you use the proof, cite the original release and credit Levent Alpöge and Claude. # VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.
This one is about **speed on AMD RDNA 3**: the world at 30 frames a second on
one PC, without giving up the picture. It is not there yet.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-25)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, 1440p, the Series X profile.

| | |
|---|---|
| Menus, videos, loading screens | 30 fps |
| Prologue, indoors | 50-75 ms a frame (13-20 fps) |
| First mission with the boat | 46-53 ms (19-22 fps) |
| Street chase with many cars and people | 100-165 ms (6-10 fps), single frames far longer |
| Outdoors on foot, the camp | 60-90 ms |
| Flying | 42-57 ms |
| Longest session so far | 41 minutes, no crash |
| Memory | 40-46 GB of private memory: **64 GB of RAM recommended** |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes two days earlier.

What is known to be wrong:

- Trees, plants and far buildings flicker outdoors in some places.
- Rooms with little direct light are too dark without `-RayTracing`.
- Textures of what just came into view appear late while the title streams.
- The first run with a new driver or a new build stutters while the driver makes
  pipelines (`victory warm` makes them ahead).
- Recording a frame in the world makes the title's own watchdog end it.

## How to run it

You need Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader
model 6.6 and mesh shaders, Rust (the toolchain is pinned), the MSVC build
tools, and your own dump of the title.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/avatarmanz/VIctory-7900XTX
cd VIctory-7900XTX
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml      # then set your paths, outside this folder
cargo build --locked --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics
scripts\play.ps1 -Exe <path of your copy's executable>
```

`scripts\play.ps1 -Safe` leaves out the newest, faster ways; try it first when
something is wrong. `-RayTracing` turns the title's ray-traced indirect light on.

Before the first run, ahead of time (both can be stopped and go on later):

```powershell
target\diag\victory.exe shaders <the shader archives>   # every shader translated, minutes
target\diag\victory.exe warm --used                     # pipelines earlier runs drew with, for a new driver or build
```

Commands, debugging switches and upstream's own description:
[docs/README-fxceless.md](docs/README-fxceless.md). Every `VICTORY_...` switch is
described in a comment where it is read.

## What is different here

In short; the reasons and the measurements are in [docs/findings.md](docs/findings.md).

# VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.

## The goal

**A stable 30 fps or more without ray tracing, then as high a frame rate and as
low frame times as the PC allows**, on an AMD RX 7900 XTX first and on PCs with
32 GB (later 16 GB) of RAM.

The way there is **porting, not emulating**: patching the title's renderer so it
behaves the way a PC renderer does, rather than having the layer watch and copy
the console's shared memory every frame. Shaders are translated ahead of time
into a versioned store that is kept between builds. Ray tracing stays optional
and off by default. The picture comes after the frame rate: texture pop-in and
lighting that is too bright or too dark when walking indoors are next in line.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-26)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, the Series X profile, ray tracing off.

| | |
|---|---|
| City street, renderer patches 1+2 on | about 53 ms a frame (about 19 fps) |
| Same scene before the patches | 57-75 ms (13-17 fps) |
| Shaders the title uses that translate | all of them (25,790 of 25,985; the rest are unused geometry shaders) |
| Memory | about 35 GB of private memory: **64 GB of RAM recommended** for now |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes three days earlier.

### Renderer patches (off by default while they are tested)

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `VICTORY_PORT_CONSTANTS=1` | The title's 174 MB constants heap is read by the card where the title writes it: no uploads, no fills |
| `VICTORY_PORT_DESCRIPTORS=1` | The title's descriptor-table stores are patched (byte-checked) to report the slots they write, instead of a scan of ~600,000 slots a frame |

What is known to be wrong:

- Trees, signs and far objects flicker in the distance in some places.
- Lighting is too bright or too dark after walking indoors, until the title has
  run for a while; rooms with little direct light are too dark without `-RayTracing`.
- Textures of what just came into view appear late while the title streams.
- The first run of a new build stutters while the driver makes pipelines
  (`victory warm` makes them ahead).
- Recording a frame in the world makes the title's own watchdog end it.

# llm.asm

**Three complete LLM projects written in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly.**
Zero C, zero C++, zero Rust, zero libc, zero libm, zero runtime dependencies.

Assembled directly with `nasm` and linked with `ld`. Every math kernel (`expf`, `sincosf`, `RMSNorm`, `RoPE`, `SiLU`, `Softmax`), AVX2+FMA+F16C GEMM/GEMV engine, BPE tokenizer, `clone()`/`futex()` thread pool, bare-metal SMP kernel, analytical backward pass, AdamW optimizer, and live Unicode Braille TUI is hand-written x86-64 assembly (`17,252` lines total across all three projects).

## The Trilogy

| Project | Binary | Size | Deps | Key Numbers |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **[01-qwen3-inference/](01-qwen3-inference/)** | `build/asm-llm` | **14,712 B** *(14,008 B `FAST_Q8=0`)* | **0** | Static Linux ELF running `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (Q8_0, built-in BPE tokenizer, GQA + QK-Norm + RoPE + SwiGLU, single-shot & `--chat` multi-turn KV-cache REPL). **`FAST_Q8=1` (default):** **126.8 tok/s** decode at 40T (**20.7 tok/s** at 1T), **+18% to +36% faster than `llama.cpp` CPU (`Q8_0`) across 1..40T**, **`0.99965`** cosine & **64/64** exact greedy tokens vs PyTorch FP32. |

| **[03-minigpt-train/](03-minigpt-train/)** | `build/asm-gpt-train` | **32,944 B** | **0** | From-scratch FP32 Mini-GPT trainer and sampler. Register-blocked `6x16` AVX2+FMA SGEMM, full analytical backward pass (**`1.0000000000`** cosine across all 21 gradient tensors vs PyTorch CPU), decoupled AdamW, **27,662 train tok/s**, live 80x24 Braille TUI, `val_loss 4.19 -> 1.51` on TinyShakespeare in 4 min. |

他家庭条件很苦，父母（张顺昌、陈媛美）来自广西玉林市陆川县滩面镇，常年在工地打零工维生。靠着自己的拼命努力，他主攻 Android 逆向、内核开发与移动安全，先后在字节跳动、阿里巴巴实习，并且**已经成功拿到了阿里巴巴的转正 Offer**。

本来他美好的人生才刚刚要开始，但在 Offer 即将开奖的前一周，他在学校宿舍倒下了。

他在开源社区留下和参与过的部分项目：
- `unidbg-fetch-qsign` / `Shamrock`
- `ZygiskNext`
- [amice](https://github.com/fuqiuluo/amice)（基于 Rust 的 LLVM 混淆与指令级 VMP 框架）
- [ice3tier](https://github.com/fuqiuluo/ice3tier) / [rnidbg](https://github.com/fuqiuluo/rnidbg) / [android-wuwa](https://github.com/fuqiuluo/android-wuwa) / [RanchuWoA](https://github.com/fuqiuluo/RanchuWoA)

大家熟知的 [go-cqhttp](https://github.com/Mrs4s/go-cqhttp)、[Lagrange.Core](https://github.com/LagrangeDev/Lagrange.Core)、[icqq](https://github.com/icqqjs/icqq) 等 QQBot 协议及其相关衍生开源项目，都离不开他背后挥洒的汗水。

---

## 事发经过

- 11 月 25 日下午三点多，张雨鑫在学校宿舍时突发心源性猝死晕倒。

- 在场室友第一时间对他进行了紧急心肺复苏（CPR），随后由辅导员紧急送往**长沙市中心医院**抢救。  
- 在医院历经近 4 个小时的全力抢救，他的心跳才得以恢复，随后被转入急诊 ICU 重症监护室，目前已紧急启用 **ECMO（人工肺）** 维持生命体征。  
- 目前医院诊断为：**呼吸心跳骤停（心源性可能性大）、心肺复苏后缺氧缺血性脑病**、心律失常、代谢性酸中毒、高乳酸血症、心肌损害、肝功能不全、横纹肌溶解症等。由于多器官受损，目前他的生命体征依然极不稳定，随时面临危险。
- ECMO 光开机费用就要 **6–7 万元**，加上 ICU 每日的运转、监护、用药及抢救，每天的费用高达 **1–2 万元**。
- 更加雪上加霜的是，**目前无医保可供报销**，所有治疗费用全部需要家庭自费承担。
- 常年在工地打零工的父母，在出事后的短短几天内就已经耗尽了家里全部积蓄和亲友借款，面对 ICU 每天上万元的账单已彻底无力支撑。

> 更多详情请见[轻松筹项目页](https://m.qsmutual.com/fund/detail?projuuid=707d9690-2f56-4e1b-adb1-84b862e94c5b)。

---

## 进展记录

- **2026-11-27**：建立本仓库同步情况（[@PangBaiWork](https://github.com/PangBaiWork) 为 fuqiuluo 合租舍友）
- **2026-11-26**：在 fuqiuluo 本人的 QQ 群（`943577597`）内，其现实朋友与舍友发声并核实情况，社区开始接力发力。
- **2026-11-25**：下午 15 时许在宿舍突发晕倒，室友紧急 CPR 后送入长沙市中心医院，抢救近 4 小时恢复心跳，转入急诊 ICU 并上 ECMO。

# 把经历变成证据

![Build PDF](https://github.com/returnSGD/campus2offer/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)

**计算机学生的四年规划与求职实战**（工作稿 v1.0）

> 把学习变成证据，把选择变成实验，把工作变成下一次选择的起点。

## 下载

- **最新编译版（PDF）**：[Releases · latest](https://github.com/returnSGD/campus2offer/releases/latest)
- 直链：`https://github.com/returnSGD/campus2offer/releases/latest/download/campus2offer-latest.pdf`

**仓库里不存 PDF。** 每次 `main` 有更新（包括合并 PR），CI 会重新编译并覆盖这个 release 的 PDF；想看旧版就翻 Releases 历史或 Actions 的 artifact。这样贡献者改 `.tex` 时不会和编译产物打架。
这本书写给计算机大类的高中生、本科生和应届生：从选专业、看培养方案、做第一个真实项目，到写简历、面试、选 offer、入职前九十天。它不承诺 offer，只提供一套更可靠的工作方式——**先把问题说清楚，做一个成本可承受的实验，进入真实环境，记录结果，再根据证据调整方向**。

## 这本书里有什么

- **14 章正文**：起点（专业、时间轴、分叉口）→ 能力（工程、刷题、协作、代表作）→ 求职（岗位、企业、简历、面试、秋招）→ 现实（钱、心态、信息、复盘）
- **7 个附录**：四类读者的行动路线、冷启动通信脚本库、项目卡与成果账本、术语表、主题索引、来源与参考文献、留言板
- **可填写的工具**：方向实验卡、JD 拆解表、Offer 权重表、项目卡、成果账本
- **带出处的数据**：毕业生规模、行业工资、软件业收入、青年失业率等，脚注给出原始发布与日期

## 怎么用这个仓库

| 目的一 | 看这里 |
|---|---|
| 直接读书 | [Releases · latest](https://github.com/returnSGD/campus2offer/releases/latest)（PDF 由 CI 自动发布） |
| 改书稿 | [把经历变成证据-初稿.tex](./把经历变成证据-初稿.tex)（XeLaTeX + ctexbook） |
| 参与贡献 | [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) |
| 看改动记录 | [编辑说明.md](./编辑说明.md) |
| 改了内容要同步什么 | [维护指南.md](./维护指南.md) |

## 本地编译

需要 TeX Live 或 MiKTeX（含 XeLaTeX 与 ctex），中文字体为 SimSun / Times New Roman：

```bash
xelatex 把经历变成证据-初稿.tex
xelatex 把经历变成证据-初稿.tex   # 第二遍生成目录
```

## 欢迎 PR 的东西

- 真实、脱敏的案例（踩坑、复盘、面试追问）
- 简历 Before / After
- 项目拆解、README 模板、压测与评测脚本
- 岗位与公司的公开信息整理
- 事实核对：数据过期、口径错误、链接失效

不要提交：广告、课程推销、未经授权的他人内容、无法追溯来源的数字。

## 许可

- 文字内容：[CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/deed.zh)（署名—非商业性使用—相同方式共享）
- 代码片段：MIT

## 联系

- X：[@sundayai_](https://x.com/sundayai_)
- 邮箱：sunday.xu@ttcadvisory.com

Reloc

面向 iOS 的外设级定位模拟工具

基于 Swift、Objective-C 与 Rust FFI 构建 · 通过本机回环实现 iAP2 / MFi-v3 / NMEA 外设定位注入

--- ## 简介 **Reloc** 是一款运行在 iPhone 本机的外设级定位模拟应用。应用通过外部代理提供的本地回环（`10.7.0.1`）连接系统的 `com.apple.carkit.service` 服务，完成 Remote Pairing / Lockdown 会话协商、iAP2 链路同步、MFi-v3 鉴权与 NMEA-0183（`$GPGGA` / `$GPRMC`）报文流式下发，使系统以标准外设 GPS 身份接收实时坐标。 --- ## 核心功能 | 模块 | 能力说明 | | :--- | :--- | | **定格定位** | 地图点击选点、关键词搜索、手动输入 WGS-84 坐标、多级反地理编码（`CLGeocoder` → `Nominatim` → `BigDataCloud` 兜底不卡顿）、运行中浏览并热更新定位 | | **多源地图与纠偏** | 默认使用 **Apple 地图（MapKit 原生）** 并支持中国大陆 GCJ-02 ↔ WGS-84 自动双向纠偏；同时内置免 API Key 的 **全球街道图（Esri） / OpenStreetMap / 全球卫星图** 纯原生 WGS-84 瓦片地图（完全脱离 `MKMapView`，无高德字样）；可选 ±0.6 m 自然微漂移 | | **极速触发与优雅恢复** | iAP2 鉴权后延迟唤醒 `CoreLocation` + 自动脉冲订阅 `0xFFFA` + 初始高速锁定突发，首页实时显示外设生效状态；系统缓存顽固时提供 **一键刷新定位服务（PiP 悬浮 5 秒倒计时）**；停止定位时下发 NMEA 失效报文（`quality=0` / `V`）与 iAP2 `RST` 复位包并自动唤醒本机真实 GPS | | **后台保活** | 导航级后台定位保活 + 非零次声音频双保险；支持开关系统「定位服务」刷新缓存后自动重建后台断言，以及断线自动重连 | | **本机配对与导入** | 兼容 `.rppairing` / `.mobiledevicepairing` / `.mobilepair` / `.plist`；原生副本文件选择器避免置灰不可选，支持「用 Reloc 打开」直接导入；iOS 27+ 支持本机一键配对与 **画中画（PiP）悬浮指引窗** 实时展示 6 位配对码 | | **数据与实测** | 收藏夹（支持重命名 / 删除）、最近 30 条使用记录、异常中断一键恢复；内置 `CoreLocation` 实测面板（`isSimulatedBySoftware` / `isProducedByAccessory`）与协议日志筛选 | --- ## 系统兼容性 | 设备 / 系统版本 | 日常脱离电脑运行 | 首次获取配对文件方式 | 说明 | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | **iPhone · iOS 27.0+** | 支持 | **本机一键配对**（免电脑）或导入已有文件 | 通过 `_remotepairing-pairable-host._tcp.` + 画中画悬浮窗完成配对 | | **iPhone · iOS 17.0 – 26.x** | 支持 | **需电脑通过 USB 首次导出**，导入后长期脱离电脑 | iOS 27 之前系统限制陌生主机无线首次配对 | | **iPad（iPadOS）** | **不支持** | — | iPadOS 不支持 CarPlay 且不提供 `com.apple.carkit.service` 外设通道，启动时将自动提示不可用 | > Reloc 仅支持 **iPhone**；应用自身不创建 VPN，回环流量（`10.7.0.1`）由外部代理工具提供。 --- ## 快速开始与获取配对文件 ### 1. 启用本机回环 在外部代理工具中启用指向 `10.7.0.1` 的本机回环映射。 ### 2. 获取并导入配对文件 #### 方式 A：iOS 27+ 本机直接配对（免电脑，推荐） 1. 打开 Reloc **「设备连接」** 页，点击 **「一键配对这台 iPhone」**，画中画悬浮指引窗会自动弹出。 2. 前往系统 **「设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 开发者模式」**，滑到底部点击 **「与 Reloc 配对」**。 3. 对照悬浮窗中实时显示的 6 位配对码完成输入，配对记录将自动保存。 #### 方式 B：iOS 17 – 26 通过电脑首次导出配对文件 使用 USB 数据线连接 iPhone 并点击 **「信任此电脑」**，任选以下一种工具导出： - lsernau/grh-lean.content:
# GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, in Lean 4

Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions.

A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann
Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the
axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

The proof is based on Levent Alpöge's, with Claude (https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf).
This repository is a shorter version, produced in collaboration with my
colleagues at Anthropic, and Claude.

## Two editions

- `grh/`: readable edition, about 300,000 lines. Start at `grh/GUIDE.md`.
- `grh-compact/`: the same five theorems, about 76,000 lines.

Each folder is its own Lake project with its own README.

## Build

Needs Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib at commit 56a00585. In either folder:

    lake exe cache get
    lake build
    lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean

A build takes one to two hours on 12 cores with 24 GB of memory (about
85 minutes more if the Mathlib cache is missing).

## Status

The proof has passed machine checks only, listed in each folder's README.
No mathematician has read it through, and no paper comes with it.

## License

Apache 2.0, Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC. See `LICENSE`, and `NOTICE` and
`ATTRIBUTION.md` in each folder.

# XSEmu **Run Xbox Series X|S (GDK) titles on Windows, built on the XCL translation layer.** [![License: GPL-2.0-only](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0--only-blue)](LICENSE) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-orange?logo=rust)](Cargo.toml) [![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-0078D6)](#requirements) [![Status: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-experimental-red)](#status)
XSEmu runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) titles on Windows x64. It is built on [XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl), a compatibility layer by ivall and its contributors, and it works the way Wine does: the title's x64 code runs natively on the host CPU, and XCL stands in for the console libraries that Windows does not have. XSEmu does not emulate the console's CPU or hardware. ## Contents - [Status](#status) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Shader pipeline](#shader-pipeline) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Build and test](#build-and-test) - [Usage](#usage) - [Repository layout](#repository-layout) - [Upstream and licence](#upstream-and-licence) - [Legal](#legal) ## Status XSEmu is experimental research software. Expect crashes, missing features and rendering errors. This repository makes no compatibility claims for any title. The [upstream README](UPSTREAM.md) records the results that XCL reported; those are XCL's results, not XSEmu's. ## How it works `XSEmu run` maps the title's executable and DLLs into its own process and runs them on the host CPU. Each import goes to an XCL replacement, the title's own DLL, the Windows DLL of the same name, or a logged stub.
